title: consolidate-openai-compat-tool-routing-and-output-normalization
author: Ravi Patel
release_notes: Normalize OpenAI-compatible tool calling: server-side schema mapper, deterministic tool_choice fallback, and streaming message envelope to avoid fragmented tool payloads. Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in flag added for strict v2 schema.
description:
Motivation: Our OpenAI compatibility layer currently exposes two pain points for customers using function/tool calling: 1) model-provided tool schemas don't map cleanly to Redwood internal tool descriptors (naming/param shapes), and 2) streaming tool invocations occasionally emit fragmented or partial tool messages over SSE which breaks downstream tool runners and observability. This PR implements a server-side schema normalization layer, a clearer tool_choice fallback heuristic, and a streaming envelope so tool messages are only emitted when complete.

What this changes (high level):
- Add a schema mapper that translates OpenAI-style 'functions' definitions into Redwood's internal tool descriptor format, with field aliasing, type coercion rules, and a validation step. The mapper supports a small rule set (rename map, required->optional normalization, array<->single coercion) and is extensible.
- Implement explicit tool_choice semantics: when a model returns an explicit tool selection we prefer it; when the model returns ambiguous 'tool' or partial name we run a deterministic resolver that prefers exact-name matches, then best fuzzy match, then a configured fallback tool (configurable per-tenant). This removes flakiness seen when models return partial names or alternate case.
- Streaming stability: updated stream_chunker to buffer tool invocation events and emit a single 'tool_invocation' envelope once the tool message is fully assembled. The envelope includes the normalized schema name and a checksum header to allow downstream deduplication. This prevents clients from receiving half-formed JSON that can break tool runners.
- OpenAI-compat API shape: the OpenAI-compatible responses now include an optional 'tool_invocation' key (when applicable) alongside the usual 'choices' array; inside the streaming protocol, we emit a sentinel chunk with 'tool_invocation:ready' to mark the finalization of a tool payload. Backwards compatibility: the old behavior is still available behind the feature flag openai_compat.tool_message_schema_v1=false (default is true->new behavior).
- Tests and docs: add unit tests for the mapper, deterministic resolver, and stream chunking; add integration e2e test that simulates a model returning ambiguous tool names and ensures the right tool is run plus a docs page describing migration and opt-in flag.

Commits (high level):
- feat(openai_compat): add schema mapper and normalization rules
- feat(runtime): deterministic tool_choice resolver with tenant fallback config
- fix(streaming): buffer partial tool messages and emit final envelope
- test: unit and integration tests for mapper/resolver/streaming
- docs: openai-tool-compat migration guide and examples

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/openai_compat/mapper.go - new mapping and validation logic
- pkg/openai_compat/mapper_test.go - unit tests for schema mapping
- pkg/runtime/tool_choice_resolver.go - resolver and heuristics
- pkg/runtime/tool_choice_resolver_test.go - unit tests
- pkg/serve/stream_chunker.go - buffer/envelope changes for streaming
- pkg/serve/tool_invocation.go - runtime handling for normalized tool invocations
- sdk/python/openai_compat.py - client-side docstrings and a helper for backwards compatibility toggles
- docs/openai-tool-compat.md - migration notes and examples
- tests/integration/test_tool_streaming.py - e2e simulating ambiguous tool names
- tests/e2e/fixtures/ambiguous_tool_model.json - simulated model output

CI and iteration notes:
- CI run initially failed on tests/integration/test_tool_streaming.py due to an off-by-one in the chunker boundary detection. The failing test reproduced locally and the boundary fix was pushed in commit 'fix(streaming): adjust chunker flush condition'. After that all CI jobs (unit, integration, lint) passed.

Review summary (selected conversation snippets):
- Amir Hassan: "The mapper looks good; please add a small table of supported coercions in the docs and ensure we log mappings at info level for the first N requests to help troubleshoot."
- Author (Ravi): "Added coercion table in docs and a sampled_info_log in mapper.go gated by tenant sampling config."
- Lucia Gomez: "Resolver should not rely on fuzzy matching for high-sensitivity tenants. Can we honor a per-tenant strict_mode?"
- Author: "Added tenant strict_mode override; strict_mode disables fuzzy matching and falls back to configured default tool or a clear error that surfaces to observability."
- Dana Lee: "What are the perf implications of buffering tool messages?"
- Author: "Measured impact: median token latency unchanged; p95 increased by ~6ms for tool-heavy sessions due to buffering. Added telemetry metric (openai_compat.tool_stream_buffer_ms) and included it in the console dashboard tile for monitoring."

Migration and compatibility:
- Default behavior: new normalized tool_envelope is enabled for all new deployments. We provide a toggled config key openai_compat.tool_message_schema_v1 (true to keep old behavior). Tenant admins in Dedicated/Private can opt out until they update their tool runners.
- The PR includes docs with examples showing how to update tool runners to accept the normalized envelope and how to enable strict_mode to avoid fuzzy matches.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: some customers relied on receiving partial tool stdout and may break if they expected stream fragments. Mitigation: feature flag and migration docs; we will monitor errors and offer a migration support window.
- Risk: fuzzy matching could select incorrect tools. Mitigation: strict_mode and telemetry to surface resolver confidence; also sampling logs for ambiguous resolutions.

Merge: squashed and merged after approvals from reviewers listed above. Release note added to changelog under 2025-11 patch.
